How many shipments by truck were made?

Evidence:
shipment by truck refers to Name = 'XRQ - TRUCK GROUND';
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ShipMethod AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS T2 USING (ShipMethodID) WHERE T1.Name = 'XRQ - TRUCK GROUND'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Begin with the shipping-method table, which contains the method name specified in the evidence: `FROM ShipMethod AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each shipping method to the sales orders shipped with that method through their shared identifier: `INNER JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS T2 USING (ShipMethodID)`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined order records to the truck-ground shipping method: `WHERE T1.Name = 'XRQ - TRUCK GROUND'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Count every matching sales-order row, since each joined row represents a shipment using that method: `COUNT(*)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Place the aggregate count in the query’s projection before the joined tables and filter: `SELECT COUNT(*)`.

answer: SELECT lname FROM faculty WHERE rank  =  'Professor' EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT T1.lname FROM Faculty AS T1 JOIN Faculty_participates_in AS T2 ON T1.facID  =  T2.facID JOIN activity AS T3 ON T2.actid  =  T2.actid WHERE T3.activity_name  =  'Canoeing' OR T3.activity_name  =  'Kayaking'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Build the initial result set by selecting the `lname` values of faculty members whose rank is Professor: `SELECT lname FROM faculty WHERE rank = 'Professor'`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Create the participation-side relation by linking faculty members to their activity participation records through `facID`: `FROM Faculty AS T1 JOIN Faculty_participates_in AS T2 ON T1.facID = T2.facID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Extend the participation relation to the activity table using the activity identifier condition from the target query: `JOIN activity AS T3 ON T2.actid = T2.actid`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Restrict participating faculty to those associated with either Canoeing or Kayaking: `WHERE T3.activity_name = 'Canoeing' OR T3.activity_name = 'Kayaking'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Use set difference to remove the distinct last names returned by the participation-side query from the Professor result set, beginning the second projection with: `EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT T1.lname`.

Question:
Name the state with the most number of graduate cohort in 2012 from private institute for profit? List all such institutes in the mentioned state.

Evidence:
most number of graduate cohort refers to MAX(SUM(grad_cohort)); in 2012 refers to year = 2012; private institute for profit refers to control = 'Private for-profit'; institutes refers to chronname;
answer: SELECT T1.state, T1.chronname FROM institution_details AS T1 INNER JOIN state_sector_grads AS T2 ON T1.state = T2.state WHERE T2.year = 2012 AND T1.control = 'Private for-profit' GROUP BY T2.grad_cohort ORDER BY COUNT(T2.grad_cohort) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Connect each institution to state-level graduation records through the shared state value: `FROM institution_details AS T1 INNER JOIN state_sector_grads AS T2 ON T1.state = T2.state`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the graduation records to the requested reporting year, 2012: `WHERE T2.year = 2012`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Extend the filter to retain institutions whose control type is private for-profit: `AND T1.control = 'Private for-profit'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Group by graduate cohort and rank the groups by their record counts from highest to lowest: `GROUP BY T2.grad_cohort ORDER BY COUNT(T2.grad_cohort) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the state and institution name, then retain only the top-ranked result: `SELECT T1.state, T1.chronname` and `LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the active employees, how many of them have a courtesy title of "Mr"?

Evidence:
active status of employees refers to CurrentFlag = 1;
answer: SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.CurrentFlag = 1 AND T2.Title = 'Mr.'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the employee records because active status is stored in the `Employee` table: `FROM Employee AS T1`.

prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the records to active employees according to the supplied definition: `WHERE T1.CurrentFlag = 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Further restrict those active employees to people whose courtesy title is exactly `Mr.`: `AND T2.Title = 'Mr.'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Count the business entity identifiers of the employees satisfying both conditions in the projection: `SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID)`.

answer: SELECT AVG(T3.length) FROM actor AS T1 INNER JOIN film_actor AS T2 ON T1.actor_id = T2.actor_id INNER JOIN film AS T3 ON T2.film_id = T3.film_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'PENELOPE' AND T1.last_name = 'GUINESS'

Question:
Of all the All-star players who played in the Eastern Conference for no more than 5 minutes, how many went to Illinois College?

Evidence:
Eastern conference refers to conference = 'East'; no more than 5 minutes refers to minutes < 5
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.playerID) FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN player_allstar AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.conference = 'East' AND T2.minutes <= 5 AND T1.college = 'Illinois'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from player biographical records and link them to All-Star appearances through the shared player identifier: `FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN player_allstar AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the All-Star appearances to players in the Eastern Conference: `WHERE T2.conference = 'East'`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Apply the specified playing-time threshold so that only appearances lasting no more than five minutes qualify: `AND T2.minutes <= 5`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Limit the qualifying players to those whose recorded college is Illinois: `AND T1.college = 'Illinois'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Count unique player identifiers so a player with multiple qualifying All-Star appearances is counted only once: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.playerID)`.

prefix_hints.hint_4: Sort the joined rows by invoice total in ascending order so the cheapest invoices appear first: `ORDER BY total`.

Question:
Which vendor's selling price for Hex Nut 5 is the lowest, please give the vendor's name.

Evidence:
vendor's selling price refers to StandardPrice; lowest selling price = MIN(StandardPrice)
answer: SELECT T3.Name FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.Name = 'Hex Nut 5' ORDER BY T1.StandardPrice LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from `ProductVendor`, which stores each vendor-product relationship and its selling price in `StandardPrice`: `FROM ProductVendor AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join `Product` so the vendor-product records can be matched to the requested product by its name: `INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Join `Vendor` through the shared business entity identifier to retrieve the vendor's name: `INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Restrict the records to the product named Hex Nut 5: `WHERE T2.Name = 'Hex Nut 5'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the vendor name, sort by selling price from lowest to highest, and retain the cheapest result using these clauses: `SELECT T3.Name`, `ORDER BY T1.StandardPrice LIMIT 1`.

Question:

Evidence:
American Airlines Inc. refers to Description = 'American Airlines Inc.: AA'; on 2018/8/1 refers to FL_DATE = '2018/8/1'; faster than scheduled refers to ACTUAL_ELAPSED_TIME < CRS_ELAPSED_TIME;
answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.ACTUAL_ELAPSED_TIME < CRS_ELAPSED_TIME THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count FROM Airports AS T1 INNER JOIN Airlines AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.ORIGIN INNER JOIN `Air Carriers` AS T3 ON T2.OP_CARRIER_AIRLINE_ID = T3.Code WHERE T2.FL_DATE = '2018/8/1' AND T3.Description = 'American Airlines Inc.: AA'

prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined flight records to the requested date: `WHERE T2.FL_DATE = '2018/8/1'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Add the carrier-description condition so that only flights operated by American Airlines Inc. remain: `AND T3.Description = 'American Airlines Inc.: AA'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Count qualifying flights by conditionally contributing 1 when actual elapsed time is less than scheduled elapsed time, and 0 otherwise: `SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.ACTUAL_ELAPSED_TIME < CRS_ELAPSED_TIME THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count`.

Question:
What is the total ordered quantity for products under the 'Touring' line?

Evidence:
The Touring line refers to the product line, therefore ProductLine = 'T'
answer: SELECT SUM(T2.OrderQty) FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T1.ProductLine = 'T'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start with the `Product` table because it contains the `ProductLine` attribute used to identify Touring products: `FROM Product AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each product to its purchase-order detail records through the shared product identifier: `INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined records to the Touring product line, represented by the code `T`: `WHERE T1.ProductLine = 'T'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Aggregate the ordered quantities from all qualifying purchase-order detail rows: `SUM(T2.OrderQty)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Use the aggregate expression as the query projection, then place it before the product source, join, and Touring filter clauses: `SELECT SUM(T2.OrderQty)`.

Question:
Please list the top 3 house-manufactured products with the highest average rating.

Evidence:
home manufactured refers to MakeFlag = 1; average rating = divide(sum(Rating), count(ProductReview))
answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY SUM(T1.Rating) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Connect each review to its product so the product name and manufacturing flag are available alongside the rating: `FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the joined records to products manufactured in-house, represented by `MakeFlag = 1`: `WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Create one result group for each product name so its review ratings can be aggregated: `GROUP BY T2.Name`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Rank the grouped products by the sum of their ratings in descending order, as specified by the target query: `ORDER BY SUM(T1.Rating) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the product name and retain only the highest-ranked result by placing `SELECT T2.Name` at the beginning and `LIMIT 1` after the ordering clause.

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start with the table containing the male people whose names will be counted: `FROM male AS T1`.

prefix_hints.hint_3: Use the evidence mapping to retain people whose payment status is represented by `neg`: `WHERE T2.bool = 'neg'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Count the qualifying male names after the join and filter have been applied: `COUNT(T1.name)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Place the aggregate count in the query’s projection before the previously constructed clauses: `SELECT COUNT(T1.name)`.

Question:
What is the weight in pounds of the style that is produced the most by the company? If there are multiple products sharing the same weight, indicate the name of each one of them and their corresponding weights.

Evidence:
weight in pounds refers to WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB';
answer: SELECT Weight FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB' GROUP BY Weight ORDER BY COUNT(Style) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Use the `Product` table because it contains product weights, styles, and weight-unit codes: `FROM Product`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the products to those whose weights are measured in pounds, as indicated by the `LB` unit code: `WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB'`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Group the pound-denominated products by weight so that style occurrences can be counted for each distinct weight: `GROUP BY Weight`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Rank the weight groups by their number of non-null style values, placing the most frequently produced group first: `ORDER BY COUNT(Style) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Return the weight from only the highest-ranked group by using the projection and row limit: `SELECT Weight` and `LIMIT 1`.

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the client records because the female condition is stored in the `gender` column: `FROM client AS T1`.

prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined records to female clients using the provided gender mapping: `WHERE T1.gender = 'F'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Add the target average-salary range using district column `A11`: `AND T2.A11 BETWEEN 6000 AND 10000`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Count distinct district identifiers so each qualifying district contributes only once: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.district_id)`.

Question:
what is the smallest state that the mississippi river runs through
answer: SELECT state_name FROM state WHERE area  =  ( SELECT MIN ( area ) FROM state WHERE state_name IN ( SELECT traverse FROM river WHERE river_name  =  "mississippi" ) ) AND state_name IN ( SELECT traverse FROM river WHERE river_name  =  "mississippi" );

prefix_hints.hint_2: Among those traversed states, calculate the minimum state area using the river-state list as a membership filter: `SELECT MIN(area) FROM state WHERE state_name IN (SELECT traverse FROM river WHERE river_name = "mississippi")`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Set up the outer query to return the name of the qualifying state from the `state` table: `SELECT state_name FROM state`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Require the selected state's area to equal the minimum area calculated for Mississippi-traversed states: `WHERE area = (SELECT MIN(area) FROM state WHERE state_name IN (SELECT traverse FROM river WHERE river_name = "mississippi"))`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Also confirm that the returned state itself belongs to the set traversed by the Mississippi River: `AND state_name IN (SELECT traverse FROM river WHERE river_name = "mississippi")`.

Evidence:
good at both left hands and right hands for goalie refers to shootCatch IS NULL
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.firstName, T1.lastName FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN HOF AS T2 ON T1.hofID = T2.hofID WHERE T1.shootCatch IS NULL

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the `Master` table, which contains each player's name, catching-hand information, and Hall of Fame identifier: `FROM Master AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each player to their Hall of Fame record through the shared `hofID`: `INNER JOIN HOF AS T2 ON T1.hofID = T2.hofID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Apply the evidence definition for goalies who are good with both hands by selecting players whose `shootCatch` value is NULL: `WHERE T1.shootCatch IS NULL`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Project both name fields requested by the target result from the player record: `SELECT T1.firstName, T1.lastName`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Add deduplication to the projection so each Hall of Fame player's name appears only once: `SELECT DISTINCT T1.firstName, T1.lastName`.

Question:
What is the product with the most profit?

Evidence:
profit = SUBTRACT(ListPrice, StandardCost);
answer: SELECT T1.ProductID FROM ProductListPriceHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductCostHistory AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T1.ListPrice - T2.StandardCost DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Begin with the price-history table because it contains each product's historical `ListPrice`: `FROM ProductListPriceHistory AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join the corresponding cost-history records through the shared product identifier so each price can be compared with a standard cost: `INNER JOIN ProductCostHistory AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Calculate profit by subtracting the standard cost from the list price, following the provided definition: `T1.ListPrice - T2.StandardCost`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Rank the joined records from greatest profit to least profit: `ORDER BY T1.ListPrice - T2.StandardCost DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the product identifier and retain only the first record in the profit ranking: `SELECT T1.ProductID` and `LIMIT 1`.

Question:
What percentage is Landon Donovan's overall rating higher than Jordan Bowery on 2013/7/12?

Evidence:
Landon Donovan's refers to player_name = 'Landon Donovan'; Jordan Bowery refers to player_name = 'Jordan Bowery'; percentage refers to DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(player_name = 'Landon Donovan' overall_rating; player_name = 'Jordan Bowery' overall_rating), player_name = 'Landon Donovan' overall_rating)*100
answer: SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 - SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Jordan Bowery' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END)) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END) LvsJ_percent FROM Player AS t1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.player_fifa_api_id = t2.player_fifa_api_id WHERE SUBSTR(t2.`date`, 1, 10) = '2013-07-12'

prefix_hints.hint_3: Obtain Landon Donovan's rating for that date with conditional aggregation, using it as the comparison denominator: `SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END)`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Similarly obtain Jordan Bowery's rating so it can be subtracted from Landon Donovan's rating: `SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Jordan Bowery' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Calculate the rating difference, divide it by Landon Donovan's rating, multiply by 100, and label the result; multiplying by `1.0` ensures decimal arithmetic: `SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 - SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Jordan Bowery' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END)) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' THEN t2.overall_rating ELSE 0 END) LvsJ_percent`.

Question:
Calculate the average length of employment for employee working in the Research and Development deparment.

Evidence:
average length of employment = AVG(subtract(2022, year(HireDate)))
answer: SELECT AVG(STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate)) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T3 ON T2.DepartmentID = T3.DepartmentID WHERE T3.Name = 'Research and Development'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from employee records because `HireDate` is stored in `Employee`, then connect each employee to their department history using the shared business entity identifier: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join the department history to `Department` so that the department name is available for filtering: `INNER JOIN Department AS T3 ON T2.DepartmentID = T3.DepartmentID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined records to employees associated with the Research and Development department: `WHERE T3.Name = 'Research and Development'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Calculate each employee's employment length in years by subtracting the hire year from the current year with SQLite's `STRFTIME` function: `STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Average the calculated employment lengths by placing the year-difference expression inside `AVG` in the projection: `SELECT AVG(STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate))`.

Question:
List all staff in the Shipping and Receiving department who are hired in 2009.

Evidence:
hired in 2009 refers to year(HireDate) = 2009
answer: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009' AND T4.Name = 'Shipping and Receiving'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start with `Person` for staff names and link each person to their employee record using the shared business entity identifier: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Connect each employee to their department assignment history through `BusinessEntityID`: `INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Join the assignment history to `Department` so the department can be identified by name: `INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Restrict the results to employees hired in 2009 and assigned to Shipping and Receiving: `WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009' AND T4.Name = 'Shipping and Receiving'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the first and last names of the qualifying staff members in the SELECT clause: `SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName`.

Question:
List the name and country of the players who got more than average catches in ascending order of the number of catches.

Evidence:
name and country of the players refers to Player_Name and Country_Name; catches refers to Out_name = 'caught'; average catches refers to divide(count(Player_ID) when Out_name = 'caught', sum(Player_ID))
answer: SELECT T1.Player_Name, T4.Country_Name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Wicket_Taken AS T2 ON T1.Player_Id = T2.Fielders INNER JOIN Out_Type AS T3 ON T2.Kind_Out = T3.Out_Id INNER JOIN Country AS T4 ON T1.Country_Name = T4.Country_Id GROUP BY T1.Player_Name ORDER BY COUNT(T3.Out_Name) ASC

prefix_hints.hint_1: Connect each player to wicket records where that player appears as the fielder, allowing catches to be attributed to the correct player: `FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Wicket_Taken AS T2 ON T1.Player_Id = T2.Fielders`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join the dismissal-type lookup so each fielding dismissal has its corresponding outcome name available for counting: `INNER JOIN Out_Type AS T3 ON T2.Kind_Out = T3.Out_Id`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Link each player to the country lookup through the country identifier to retrieve the readable country name: `INNER JOIN Country AS T4 ON T1.Country_Name = T4.Country_Id`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Aggregate the joined wicket records by player, then sort players in ascending order according to their dismissal-name count: `GROUP BY T1.Player_Name ORDER BY COUNT(T3.Out_Name) ASC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the requested player and country names at the beginning of the assembled query: `SELECT T1.Player_Name, T4.Country_Name`.
